intro: Professionals and everyday users convert psi (psi) to megapascals (MPa) when working across imperial and si standards in automotive tire inflation placards, hydraulic cylinder design, scuba diving tanks, and barometric weather tracking. One pounds per square inch equals 0.006895 megapascals, while 1 megapascal equals 145.037738 psi. Whether you are verifying pressure specifications on imported equipment, cross-checking technical datasheets, or scaling practical measurements, this converter applies the exact NIST SP 811 and ISO 80000 reference relationship with instant precision.

mistakesAndEdgeCases.title: Gauge Pressure (psig) vs. Absolute Pressure (psia)
items: This converter scales pressure magnitude directly between psi and MPa. In automotive tires, HVAC, and compressed air systems, gauges display Gauge Pressure (referenced to ambient atmospheric pressure, ~14.696 psi or 101.325 kPa at sea level).
For thermodynamic gas laws (PV = nRT) or vacuum chamber calculations, convert gauge pressure to absolute pressure by adding local barometric pressure before scaling.

faqs.question: How many megapascals (MPa) are in 1 pounds per square inch (psi)?
faqs.answer: There are 0.00689476 megapascals (MPa) in 1 pounds per square inch (psi), which rounds to 0.0069 MPa for everyday calculations. Conversely, 1 megapascal equals 145.037738 psi.

faqs.question: How do I convert psi to megapascals (psi to MPa)?
faqs.answer: To convert psi to megapascals, use the formula: MPa = psi × 0.00689476. For example, converting 35 psi gives 0.2413 MPa.

faqs.question: What is 35 psi in megapascals?
faqs.answer: 35 psi (psi) equals exactly 0.2413 megapascals (MPa) using standard NIST SP 811 and ISO 80000 conversion factors.
